sections.sectionTitle: Section A: Language (Harshe / Tsarin Sauti da Nahawu)

topics.title: Comprehension, Composition, Sound System, Grammar, and Translation

subtopics.content: Reading comprehension, essay writing types, Hausa phonetics/phonology, syllable structures, word formation, word classes, grammatical categories, sentence types, and translation
subtopics.objective: Answer comprehension questions on Hausa passages[cite: 379]; write 300-word essays (narrative, descriptive, argumentative, letter writing, etc.) in official Hausa orthography[cite: 380]; identify Hausa consonants, vowels, diphthongs, syllable structures (CV, CVV, CVC), open/close syllables, and tones (high, low, falling)[cite: 380, 381]; analyze word roots, affixes, word classes (nouns, verbs, adjectives, ideophones, etc.), tenses/aspects, gender, number, and sentence structures[cite: 381, 382]; translate accurately between Hausa and English[cite: 379].

sections.sectionTitle: Section B: Literature (Adabi), Oral and Written Literature

topics.title: Literary Appreciation, Oral and Written Literature (Prose, Poetry, Drama)

subtopics.content: Literary devices, prescribed oral folktales/proverbs/riddles/poetry/traditional drama, prescribed written Hausa novels, written poems, and plays
subtopics.objective: Apply literary appreciation principles[cite: 379]; analyze prescribed oral literature texts (*Mu Sha Dariya*, *Wasannin Kwaikwayo Na Hausawa*, *Jagoran Nazarin Wakar Baka*)[cite: 382, 388]; critique prescribed written prose texts (*Maraya*)[cite: 383, 388]; analyze prescribed written poetry selections (*Gadar Zare*)[cite: 383, 388]; evaluate set written drama plays (*Malam Zalimu*)[cite: 383, 388].

subtopics.content: Greetings (Gaisuwa), discipline/upbringing (Tarbiyya), hospitality (Karimci), family life/marriage/birth/death rites, non-Islamic traditional beliefs (Bori, Camfi), traditional occupations, traditional medicine, traditional chieftaincy titles, and traditional sports/recreation
subtopics.objective: Examine Hausa greeting types, child upbringing, hospitality, marriage, naming, and death customs[cite: 383, 384]; understand traditional religious beliefs and practices[cite: 384]; identify traditional occupations (farming, blacksmithing, tanning, dyeing)[cite: 384]; evaluate traditional medicine practitioners[cite: 384]; understand political hierarchy/titles (Sarki, Hakimi, Dagaci)[cite: 384]; identify traditional sports and entertainment (Dambe, Kokawa, Kalankuwa)[cite: 385].
